about.title: A family kitchen on Bayway Drive
text: Ray Tran and Elena Garza met working the line at a seafood house in Kemah. In 2009 they opened Casa Marea in a former bait shop on Bayway Drive, with eight tables and a menu that fit on one chalkboard.

The menu is bigger now, but the cooking has not changed: Gulf shrimp and fish bought off the docks each week, tortillas pressed by hand every morning, and salsas made in small batches through the day.
about.imageAlt: The dining room, with leather chairs, wooden tables and pendant lights

team.name: Ray Tran
team.bio: Ray runs the kitchen and buys the seafood. The étouffée is his grandmother's recipe from Port Arthur.
team.imageAlt: Ray Tran in a white chef's shirt and apron, arms crossed, in the kitchen

team.name: Elena Garza
team.bio: Elena runs the dining room and the catering side, and makes every batch of salsa verde.

reviews.author: Danielle R.
reviews.text: The garlic butter shrimp is the best plate in Baytown, and the margaritas are made with real lime. We drive over from La Porte every couple of weeks.

reviews.author: Marcus T.
reviews.text: They catered our office party for 60 people. The fajita trays showed up hot and on time, and Elena set everything up herself.

reviews.author: Priya S.
reviews.text: Small, busy and friendly. The fish tacos and the étouffée are worth the wait on a Friday night.
